messages:
oliver: noticed spike in retries + latency for svc/responder-prod in us-west1-gpu around 21:02 UTC. Alerts show 5xx retries and one node (gpu-03) taking almost all connections. can anyone check ipvs/endpoint distribution?

maya: ugh, saw the console graphs. traffic shift started right after kube-proxy daemonset rolling update ~20:58. thinking ipvs scheduling/hash change?

kevin: can you paste ipvs stats from the node? `ipvsadm -Ln --stats` or `cat /proc/net/ip_vs` should show if one real server is getting sticky flows.

oliver: grabbing from gpu-03 now:
```
# ipvsadm -Ln --stats
IP Virtual Server version 1.2.1 (size=4096)
Prot LocalAddress:Port Scheduler Flags
  -> RemoteAddress:Port           Forward Weight ActiveConn InActConn
TCP  0.0.0.0:443 rr
  -> 10.10.3.12:443               Masq    1      89234      12
  -> 10.10.3.13:443               Masq    1      1200       3
  -> 10.10.3.14:443               Masq    1      99         1
```
so yeah, 10.10.3.12 is getting 98% of packets.
```

jin: that looks like per-destination hashing pinned most flows to one real server. Did the kube-proxy version change scheduler? which kube-proxy image shows in the DS?

maya: DS is `kube-proxy:v1.27.1` rolled 20:57. previous was v1.26.5. release notes mentioned an ipvs conntrack ordering fix (might affect consistent hashing).

kevin: can we check endpoints ordering and node affinity? `kubectl get endpoints responder-prod -o yaml` and `kubectl get pods -o wide` — maybe the endpoints list has duplicates (stale addresses) or endpoint slices with uneven weights.

oliver: endpoints look normal, 3 pods across 3 IPs. interestingly, `kubectl get endpoints responder-prod -o jsonpath='{.subsets[*].addresses[*].nodeName}'` prints `gpu-03 gpu-03 gpu-04` — why is gpu-03 listed twice?

jin: aha. that suggests endpoint slices or readiness controller duplicated an address entry (likely due to kube-proxy processing an old endpoint slice plus new one). ipvs uses the endpoint list order when mapping to realservers for rr scheduler, so duplicates will skew.

kevin: also check conntrack pinning: existing persistent connections in ipvs table may keep mapping to that backend. try `conntrack -L -p tcp --orig-port-dst 443 | head` to see heavy entries.

oliver: ran `conntrack -L | wc -l` — high count (~120k) on gpu-03, compared to 8k on gpu-04. Many entries are SYN_RECV/ESTABLISHED.

maya: operational mitigation: cordon + drain gpu-03 to move pods and clear local conntrack/ipvs tables. we should also roll kube-proxy back to 1.26.5 on a small canary to validate.

kevin: agree. before drain, let's remove the problematic endpoint duplicate in the control plane if possible (delete the endpoint slice and let controller recreate) — that may reduce immediate skew. But draining will clear state for sure.

jin: another hypothesis: we recently enabled host-rdma on that node (Mellanox drivers) and an MTU mismatch on the overlay could be fragmenting flows; ipvs+RDMA path selection change combined with endpoint duplicate could amplify the skew. can infra confirm if host-rdma was toggled on gpu-03?

oliver: confirmed we enabled rdma on gpu-03 last week for a dedicated workload. there was also a small MTU bump to 9000 on the host nic but the vxlan overlay kept 1500. might be path MTU weirdness.

maya: timeline summary: kube-proxy DS updated -> endpoint slices briefly duplicated -> one node had RDMA/MTU differences -> conntrack+ipvs pinned majority of flows to one backend.

kevin: immediate plan: 1) cordon & drain gpu-03 (in maintenance window) 2) delete endpoint-slice for responder-prod to force reconcilation 3) canary rollback kube-proxy on 10% nodes to v1.26.5 4) open infra change to standardize RDMA/MTU config across GPU fleet 5) follow-up postmortem.

oliver: starting cordon now: `kubectl cordon gpu-03 && kubectl drain gpu-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force` — will report back once traffic evens out. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sre-bot: incident created: INC-2026-472 — "responder-prod uneven ipvs distribution -> retry storm" assigned to eng-infra.

maya: nice. after drain, monitor `ipvsadm -Ln --stats` on remaining nodes and console retry rates. also send a note to release engineering to pause kube-proxy rollouts until we validate behavior. :thumbsup:

kevin: logging this for postmortem: check kube-proxy logs around 20:56-21:00, endpoint-slice controller logs, and node RDMA toggles. will also search for similar reports in past 90 days.

oliver: update: 10m after drain, ipvs distribution looks even and retries dropped to baseline. Keeping the node drained until we standardize RDMA/MTU. closing this thread when postmortem links up.
